subject: USE statement
notes: The grammar writes `USE AFTER (EXCEPTION CONDITION | EC) useEcEntry+` -- one alternation, and DeclBindUseF3 is reached by `use.useEcEntry() is { Length: > 0 }` without ever inspecting which spelling was written, so the two cannot diverge by construction. The lexer note records the maximal-munch consequence that keeps EC-I-O-AT-END one IDENTIFIER rather than EC + '-I-O-AT-END'; probe ec.cob (`USE AFTER EC EC-ALL.`) and base.cob (`USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION EC-ALL.`) both compile clean. The named test is spec-derived (AssertSpec on computed output, not a legacy bake): it writes `USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION EC-ALL.` and `USE AFTER EC EC-USER-T.` in ONE program and asserts the 14.9.49.4 GR3e-before-GR3g selection -- the EC-spelled declarative is selected on its tier exactly as an EXCEPTION-CONDITION-spelled one would be, which is the synonymy claim exercised behaviourally.
